original_claim: Although quantization is often evaluated through perplexity or benchmark accuracy, those measures do not reveal whether an apparent reduction in harmful compliance is a genuine alignment change or a loss of capability.
resolved_text: Quantization evaluations commonly report perplexity or benchmark accuracy [8], [9], but those measures alone do not reveal whether an apparent reduction in harmful compliance is a genuine alignment change or a loss of capability.
evidence: The prevalence claim is now scoped to two named evaluations and cited adjacent to the sentence.

original_claim: Some methods require representative samples and an optimisation pass, while BitsAndBytes load-time quantization can be applied without a task-specific calibration set.
resolved_text: Some methods require representative samples and an optimisation pass [5], [6], [22], while BitsAndBytes load-time quantization can be applied without a task-specific calibration set [24], [25].
evidence: The calibrated and load-time method claims now carry adjacent primary-method citations.

original_claim: Prior reports of quantization-induced safety failures typically involve active adversarial jailbreaks, destructive calibration regimes, or backdoored weights, rather than standard post-training NF4 loading of unmodified instruction-tuned checkpoints.
resolved_text: Published safety findings span different settings: Kharinaev et al. and HarmLevelBench evaluate ordinary quantization [10], [29], Q-resafe uses an active decoding attack [30], and Q-Misalign studies a deliberately prepared checkpoint [33]. These designs answer different questions from standard load-time NF4 on unmodified checkpoints.
evidence: The unsupported prevalence term was replaced by an enumerated, cited comparison.
